reason: The cited evidence supports low friction and wear for the specific 2D HEA nanoflakes at room temperature and high load (E1), and mentions tribocatalytic activity. However, no evidence is provided for the formation of a stable, adaptive tribolayer at high temperatures up to 800 °C, nor for the coating's performance on a CoCrFeNi substrate under the proposed wide temperature range and variable loads. The key premise of high-temperature effectiveness is entirely unsupported.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 exhibit low friction and wear at high load in ambient air
Spray-coating is a viable method to apply these nanoflakes to a substrate
The nanoflakes exhibit stress-induced tribocatalytic activity that facilitates self-lubrication
Tribocatalytic reactions can form a protective, low-shear tribolayer on the alloy surface
The tribolayer will remain effective and stable from room temperature to 800 °C under variable loads
